key_insight: Optimizing language models with vector-valued reward signals (instead of a single scalar) produces higher-entropy, more diverse policies that improve downstream performance when used inside inference-time search procedures.
problem_solved: Standard post-training that optimizes a single scalar reward drives LLMs toward low-entropy, narrowly peaked response distributions, which hurts their ability to supply diverse rollouts needed by search-based inference methods.
method: Train policies using a vector-valued reward objective (Vector Policy Optimization) to preserve multiple task-relevant preferences rather than collapsing them into one scalar.
Encourage and preserve high-entropy, diverse response distributions during training so the model can generate a wide set of candidate rollouts at test time.
Use the trained diverse policy inside inference-time search (e.g., AlphaEvolve-style selection over rollouts) so downstream selection can pick best-performing behaviors for varied reward functions.
impact: Provides a practical training paradigm to produce LLMs that are more useful as generators inside search-based inference, improving robustness and adaptability to novel or varying task-specific reward functions.

paper_title: Vector Policy Optimization: Training for Diversity Improves Test-Time Search
